newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to UK public sector borrowing requirement data published at 0930 GMT. November's PSBR totalled 2.6 billion stg.

"In line with our forecasts. This is the best PSBR for the past five years for this year to date. The economy is gathering steam and generating more revenues. Expenditure still needs to be kept under tighter control but that's difficult in the run-up to elections. The government can certainly meet their target for this year."

"They're in line with expectations and the trend for the year to date is quite encouraging. The PSBR is well on course for hitting the Treasury's target. If the current trend is continued, the full-year deficit including privatisation proceeds could total as little as 22.5 billion stg. The inclusion of the MOD housing sale revenue in the spending figures, rather than privatisation proceeds, flatters them. And the last three months of the year tend to be the toughest in terms of controlling public spending. But the receipts side is reaping the benefit of a pick-up in activity."

"The figures were flattered slightly by the MOD proceeds but there's an encouraging inland revenue figure. Receipts continue to come in strong. That will help the PSBR at least meet the government's target and may undershoot by about a billion pounds or so."

"Certainly it appears that the overshoot which is being seen on spending is being offset by higher than had been anticipated privatisation receipts. The cumulative figures for the financial year show that, exluding privatisation proceeds, there is a borrowing requirement of 17.8 billion. This is down from 22.5 billion in the same period last year. That suggests that the government's target of 26.4 billion will be met."
